geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the monolithic cantilever into a split mass that can accept a meaningful void and preserve a clear dominant gesture.
Open a controlled central gap so the mass can respond to the public access edge with a real threshold.
Insert a courtyard derived from the dominant mass to create usable public open space.
Size the court to read as an actual spatial room rather than a thin notch.
Orient the court toward the verified access edge to establish an active ground threshold.
Wrap the existing dominant mass in a new root so the hall remains in the ancestry while the public void becomes legible.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the primary gesture by converting the existing courtyard into a more explicit carved public void tied to the access side.
Expand the void enough to read as usable public space rather than residual subtraction.
Open the court toward the verified access side in the program frame to create a legible public threshold.
Add a small entry notch so the frontage can read as a door-like seam rather than a sealed edge.
Align the entry notch with the access side.
Keep the entry incision bounded so the dominant mass remains intact.

rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant mass with decent continuity and a coherent stepped/cantilevered section, so the silhouette itself is not the main failure. However, in plan and elevation the figure is mostly a compact, sealed, tilted block with very little legible public void or ground threshold responding to the verified access edge. The thick blue frontage is met by a largely closed edge rather than an active court, seam, undercut, or entry field. That makes the program relation weak for neighborhood living, where an active ground edge and usable open space are semantic invariants. The form also feels slightly over-abstracted toward an object/mass sculpture rather than a capacity-aware street building. Reference 1 and 2 support the need for a real court or sheltered open room; reference 4 supports a grounded public base beneath upper massing. The counterfactual bridge reference should not be copied, but it does suggest a transferable operation: introduce a carved-through or bridged entry void aligned to the access side while preserving the dominant mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more facade- and canopy-led than pure massing; use only the public threshold / compact occupancy principle.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact commercial massing with a sheltered, publicly legible ground condition and a clear relationship between solid upper volume and accessible lower edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Do not copy the picturesque interior; the useful takeaway is the spatial publicness of the void.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard/void as lived public room, with mass held around an open center rather than simply carved as leftover space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is more a programmatic precedent than a massing precedent; avoid over-reading the interior rendering.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Small commercial object with a clear street-facing threshold and simple occupied interior boundary.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Typology is much taller and office-like; only the ground/public-threshold logic transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked/tapered vertical mass can still work when the base remains legible and the lower zone is civic/public.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual: too pedestrian/bridge-like and not a viable massing analog for neighborhood living; useful only as a transferable operation, not as precedent to imitate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Linear bridge-like circulation and elongated section can suggest connection across a site.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied in the visible views; no hard-gate rejection on boundary breach.
The primary access edge is visually available but not answered with a clearly public or porous ground condition.
Reference 5 is counterfactual and typologically off; use only its connective gesture as a transfer principle, not as a form model.
